text: Man is a rope stretched between the animal and the Superman—a rope over an abyss.
plain: You are mid-crossing between what you were and what you could be, and the drop below is real.

text: I tell you: one must still have chaos in one, to give birth to a dancing star. I tell you: ye have still chaos in you.
plain: The mess inside you is the raw material for something great. Don't flatten it.

text: What is great in man is that he is a bridge and not a goal: what is lovable in man is that he is an OVER-GOING and a DOWN-GOING.
plain: You are not the finished product. Being on the way to something is the point.

text: I love him who desireth not too many virtues. One virtue is more of a virtue than two, because it is more of a knot for one’s destiny to cling to.
plain: Pick one thing to be great at and hold onto it. Spread thin, nothing holds.

text: What is the greatest thing ye can experience? It is the hour of great contempt.
plain: The day you get sick of your own comfortable self is the day you can actually change.

text: Behold the good and just! Whom do they hate most? Him who breaketh up their tables of values, the breaker, the law-breaker:—he, however, is the creator.
plain: The people who follow every rule resent whoever builds something new. Expect that.

text: I make for my goal, I follow my course; over the loitering and tardy will I leap.
plain: Keep moving toward the target. Don't wait for the slow ones to catch up.

text: “We have discovered happiness”—say the last men, and blink thereby.
plain: Comfort with no goal is what the people who stopped trying call happiness.

text: Turning ill and being distrustful, they consider sinful: they walk warily. He is a fool who still stumbleth over stones or men!
plain: The safe life treats any stumble as shameful. Stumbling is how anyone gets anywhere.

text: I conjure you, my brethren, REMAIN TRUE TO THE EARTH, and believe not those who speak unto you of superearthly hopes! Poisoners are they, whether they know it or not.
plain: Put your effort into this life, this body, this day, not into someone's promise of later.

text: What is the heaviest thing, ye heroes? asketh the load-bearing spirit, that I may take it upon me and rejoice in my strength.
plain: A strong person asks for the heaviest load, because carrying it is what proves the strength.

text: What is the great dragon which the spirit is no longer inclined to call Lord and God? “Thou shalt,” is the great dragon called. But the spirit of the lion saith, “I will.”
plain: Every rule handed to you says 'you must.' Growing up means answering 'I will.'

text: Innocence is the child, and forgetfulness, a new beginning, a game, a self-rolling wheel, a first movement, a holy Yea.
plain: After the fight, you start fresh and play. Forget the old score and say yes to the work.

text: No small art is it to sleep: it is necessary for that purpose to keep awake all day.
plain: Good rest is earned by a full day of effort.

text: Ten times a day must thou overcome thyself: that causeth wholesome weariness, and is poppy to the soul.
plain: Beat your own resistance over and over every day. The tiredness that follows is the good kind.

text: Suffering was it, and impotence—that created all backworlds; and the short madness of happiness, which only the greatest sufferer experienceth.
plain: People invent a perfect other world when this one hurts and they feel helpless.

text: There is more sagacity in thy body than in thy best wisdom.
plain: Your body has its own intelligence. Don't override it with clever talk.

text: Behind thy thoughts and feelings, my brother, there is a mighty lord, an unknown sage—it is called Self; it dwelleth in thy body, it is thy body.
plain: Something deeper than your passing moods is steering. It lives in how you actually live.

text: All thy passions in the end became virtues, and all thy devils angels.
plain: Your worst drives, pointed at a real goal, become your best strengths.

text: Out of thy poisons brewedst thou balsam for thyself; thy cow, affliction, milkedst thou—now drinketh thou the sweet milk of her udder.
plain: You turned what hurt you into what feeds you.

text: Once hadst thou wild dogs in thy cellar: but they changed at last into birds and charming songstresses.
plain: Wild urges can be trained into something that sings for you.

text: He whom the flame of jealousy encompasseth, turneth at last, like the scorpion, the poisoned sting against himself.
plain: Envy ends up hurting you more than the person you envy.

text: I am a railing alongside the torrent; whoever is able to grasp me may grasp me!
plain: Support what is steady and let people lean on it if they are strong enough. Don't be their crutch.

text: Of all that is written, I love only what a person hath written with his blood. Write with blood, and thou wilt find that blood is spirit.
plain: Only work that cost you something is worth reading. Put yourself on the line.

text: Ye tell me, “Life is hard to bear.” But for what purpose should ye have your pride in the morning and your resignation in the evening?
plain: You can't be proud at breakfast and whining by dinner. Pick one.

text: Life is hard to bear: but do not affect to be so delicate! We are all of us fine sumpter asses and assesses.
plain: Yes it's heavy. Everyone is carrying a load. Stop acting too fragile for it.

text: It is true we love life; not because we are wont to live, but because we are wont to love.
plain: We love life out of love, not habit.

text: I should only believe in a God that would know how to dance.
plain: Anything worth following has to have lightness and play in it.

text: Not by wrath, but by laughter, do we slay. Come, let us slay the spirit of gravity!
plain: Beat heaviness by laughing at it, not by getting angrier.

text: Ye look aloft when ye long for exaltation; and I look downward because I am exalted.
plain: People who feel small keep looking up at others. Standing high, you look at the ground you've climbed.

text: He who climbeth on the highest mountains, laugheth at all tragic plays and tragic realities.
plain: Get high enough on your own climb and the drama down below stops moving you.

text: I learned to walk; since then have I let myself run. I learned to fly; since then I do not need pushing in order to move from a spot.
plain: Once the skill is in you, you move without being pushed.

text: The more he seeketh to rise into the height and light, the more vigorously do his roots struggle earthward, downward, into the dark and deep—into the evil.
plain: The higher you aim, the more your dark side pushes back. That's part of growing, not a sign you're failing.

text: I change too quickly: my to-day refuteth my yesterday. I often overleap the steps when I clamber; for so doing, none of the steps pardons me.
plain: Rush the climb and skip steps, and the skipped steps come back to collect.

text: When aloft, I find myself always alone. No one speaketh unto me; the frost of solitude maketh me tremble. What do I seek on the height?
plain: Climbing past people gets lonely, and you will wonder if it's worth it.

text: Maintain holy thy highest hope!
plain: Whatever else you drop, don't let go of the biggest thing you're aiming at.

text: You I advise not to work, but to fight. You I advise not to peace, but to victory. Let your work be a fight, let your peace be a victory!
plain: Treat the work as a fight you intend to win, and make your rest something you earned.

text: I know the hatred and envy of your hearts. Ye are not great enough not to know of hatred and envy. Then be great enough not to be ashamed of them!
plain: You will feel envy and hate. Admit it, then use it instead of hiding it.

text: War and courage have done more great things than charity.
plain: Bravery gets more done in the world than good intentions.

text: “What is good?” ye ask. To be brave is good.
plain: If you need a simple rule for what's good, start with courage.

text: Ye shall love peace as a means to new wars—and the short peace more than the long.
plain: Rest is for recovering before the next push. Don't sink into it.

text: Ye shall only have enemies to be hated, but not enemies to be despised. Ye must be proud of your enemies; then, the successes of your enemies are also your successes.
plain: Pick rivals worth respecting. Beating a weak one proves nothing.

text: Verily, he who possesseth little is so much the less possessed: blessed be moderate poverty!
plain: The less you own, the less owns you.

text: Towards the throne they all strive: it is their madness—as if happiness sat on the throne! Ofttimes sitteth filth on the throne.—and ofttimes also the throne on filth.
plain: The top spot is not where happiness lives, and often something rotten is sitting there.

text: Wealth they acquire and become poorer thereby. Power they seek for, and above all, the lever of power, much money—these impotent ones!
plain: Chasing money for its own sake leaves you emptier than before.

text: Flee, my friend, into thy solitude! I see thee deafened with the noise of the great men, and stung all over with the stings of the little ones.
plain: Too much noise and too many small jabs. Go be alone and recover.

text: Away from the market-place and from fame taketh place all that is great: away from the market-place and from fame have ever dwelt the devisers of new values.
plain: Great work gets made away from the crowd and the attention.

text: Slow is the experience of all deep fountains: long have they to wait until they know WHAT hath fallen into their depths.
plain: Deep things take a long time to process. Don't rush your answer to everything.

text: Raise no longer an arm against them! Innumerable are they, and it is not thy lot to be a fly-flap.
plain: Stop swatting at petty critics. There are too many, and you have better things to do.

text: Thou art not stone; but already hast thou become hollow by the numerous drops. Thou wilt yet break and burst by the numerous drops.
plain: Small constant irritations wear you down even if no single one is big.

text: What we recognise in a man, we also irritate in him.
plain: The people who bother you most are often the ones who see the real thing in you.

text: Not when the truth is filthy, but when it is shallow, doth the discerning one go unwillingly into its waters.
plain: An ugly truth is fine. A shallow one is what's worth avoiding.

text: Our faith in others betrayeth wherein we would fain have faith in ourselves. Our longing for a friend is our betrayer.
plain: What you wish others believed in you shows where you don't yet believe in yourself.

text: If one would have a friend, then must one also be willing to wage war for him: and in order to wage war, one must be CAPABLE of being an enemy.
plain: Real friendship means you'd fight for them, and that you are able to fight at all.

text: In one’s friend one shall have one’s best enemy.
plain: A good friend pushes back hard on you.

text: Art thou a tyrant? Then thou canst not have friends.
plain: If you need to rule people, you won't end up with friends, only subjects.

text: I and me are always too earnestly in conversation: how could it be endured, if there were not a friend?
plain: Alone with your own head it gets heavy. That's what a friend is for.

text: There is comradeship: may there be friendship!
plain: Having people around is easy. Having a real friend is the goal.

text: Change of values—that is, change of the creating ones. Always doth he destroy who hath to be a creator.
plain: To build something new you have to tear something old down first.

text: The one goeth to his neighbour because he seeketh himself, and the other because he would fain lose himself. Your bad love to yourselves maketh solitude a prison to you.
plain: If you can't stand your own company, being alone is a cell. Fix that first.

text: Alas! there are so many great thoughts that do nothing more than the bellows: they inflate, and make emptier than ever.
plain: Big ideas that never become action just puff you up and leave you hollow.

text: Free, dost thou call thyself? Thy ruling thought would I hear of, and not that thou hast escaped from a yoke.
plain: Escaping a boss or a rule isn't freedom. What do you now stand for?

text: Free from what? What doth that matter to Zarathustra! Clearly, however, shall thine eye show unto me: free FOR WHAT?
plain: Freedom from something is cheap. What are you free to do?

text: Terrible is aloneness with the judge and avenger of one’s own law. Thus is a star projected into desert space, and into the icy breath of aloneness.
plain: Holding yourself to your own standards with nobody watching is lonely and cold.

text: One day wilt thou see no longer thy loftiness, and see too closely thy lowliness; thy sublimity itself will frighten thee as a phantom. Thou wilt one day cry: “All is false!”
plain: There will be a day you see only your flaws and think the whole thing is a lie. Walk through it.

text: Thou goest beyond them: but the higher thou risest, the smaller doth the eye of envy see thee. Most of all, however, is the flying one hated.
plain: The further ahead you get, the more people resent you for it.

text: Injustice and filth cast they at the lonesome one: but, my brother, if thou wouldst be a star, thou must shine for them none the less on that account!
plain: They'll throw mud at you. Keep shining anyway.

text: Ready must thou be to burn thyself in thine own flame; how couldst thou become new if thou have not first become ashes!
plain: You can't become someone new without burning up the old version of you.

text: Thou lonesome one, thou goest the way to thyself! And past thyself and thy seven devils leadeth thy way!
plain: The road to who you want to be runs straight through your own demons.

text: To create, desireth the loving one, because he despiseth! What knoweth he of love who hath not been obliged to despise just what he loved!
plain: You make something better because you can't stand how it is now. That comes from love.

text: Nobler is it to own oneself in the wrong than to establish one’s right, especially if one be in the right. Only, one must be rich enough to do so.
plain: Admitting you were wrong, even when you weren't, takes a secure person.

text: Art thou the victorious one, the self-conqueror, the ruler of thy passions, the master of thy virtues? Thus do I ask thee.
plain: Before you reach for the big things, ask whether you actually rule yourself.

text: Beyond thyself shalt thou build. But first of all must thou be built thyself, rectangular in body and soul.
plain: Build yourself solid first. Everything else you make stands on that.

text: Many short follies—that is called love by you. And your marriage putteth an end to many short follies, with one long stupidity.
plain: A string of crushes isn't love, and rushing to lock it in just makes one long mistake.

text: Many never become sweet; they rot even in the summer. It is cowardice that holdeth them fast to their branches.
plain: Some people never ripen because fear keeps them clinging to where they are.

text: One must discontinue being feasted upon when one tasteth best: that is known by those who want to be long loved.
plain: Leave while they still want more.

text: Physician, heal thyself: then wilt thou also heal thy patient. Let it be his best cure to see with his eyes him who maketh himself whole.
plain: Fix yourself first. Your example does more than your advice.

text: A thousand paths are there which have never yet been trodden; a thousand salubrities and hidden islands of life. Unexhausted and undiscovered is still man and man’s world.
plain: There are still countless roads nobody has taken. Yours might be one.

text: One requiteth a teacher badly if one remain merely a scholar.
plain: The best way to honor a mentor is to go beyond them.

text: The man of knowledge must be able not only to love his enemies, but also to hate his friends.
plain: To think clearly you have to be willing to push back on the people you love.

text: Ye venerate me; but what if your veneration should some day collapse? Take heed lest a statue crush you!
plain: Putting someone on a pedestal sets you up to get crushed when they fall.

text: Now do I bid you lose me and find yourselves; and only when ye have all denied me, will I return unto you.
plain: A real teacher wants you to leave and become your own person.

text: Great obligations do not make grateful, but revengeful; and when a small kindness is not forgotten, it becometh a gnawing worm.
plain: Help that makes someone feel indebted can turn into resentment.

text: Since humanity came into being, man hath enjoyed himself too little: that alone, my brethren, is our original sin!
plain: We don't enjoy ourselves enough, and that's the real failing.

text: The worst things, however, are the petty thoughts. Verily, better to have done evilly than to have thought pettily!
plain: A small, mean thought festering inside does more damage than one honest bad act.

text: It is difficult to live among men because silence is so difficult.
plain: Most of the trouble with people comes from the things we can't keep to ourselves.

text: If, however, thou hast a suffering friend, then be a resting-place for his suffering; like a hard bed, however, a camp-bed: thus wilt thou serve him best.
plain: Give a hurting friend a place to rest, not a pillow to sink into.

text: One should hold fast one’s heart; for when one letteth it go, how quickly doth one’s head run away!
plain: Lose control of your feelings and your judgment goes right after them.

text: Ah, where in the world have there been greater follies than with the pitiful? And what in the world hath caused more suffering than the follies of the pitiful?
plain: Pity can do more harm than cruelty. Respect people enough to be hard when it helps.

text: And when a person goeth through fire for his teaching—what doth that prove! It is more, verily, when out of one’s own burning cometh one’s own teaching!
plain: Suffering for an idea proves nothing. Learning something real from your own fire does.

text: Ye love your virtue as a mother loveth her child; but when did one hear of a mother wanting to be paid for her love?
plain: Do the right thing because it's you, not for a reward.

text: With their virtues they want to scratch out the eyes of their enemies; and they elevate themselves only that they may lower others.
plain: Some people use their goodness as a weapon. Watch for it, including in yourself.

text: Distrust all those who talk much of their justice! Verily, in their souls not only honey is lacking.
plain: The loudest talkers about fairness are often hiding a grudge.

text: Spirit is life which itself cutteth into life: by its own torture doth it increase its own knowledge,—did ye know that before?
plain: You grow by cutting into your own life. Knowledge costs pain.

text: Ye know only the sparks of the spirit: but ye do not see the anvil which it is, and the cruelty of its hammer!
plain: You see the sparks. You don't see the hammering that made them.

text: Ye are not eagles: thus have ye never experienced the happiness of the alarm of the spirit. And he who is not a bird should not camp above abysses.
plain: You never feel the thrill of danger if you stay safe. And don't build your camp over a drop unless you can fly.

text: Hungry, fierce, lonesome, God-forsaken: so doth the lion-will wish itself.
plain: A strong will chooses hunger and solitude over comfort and being told what to do.

text: Free from the happiness of slaves, redeemed from Deities and adorations, fearless and fear-inspiring, grand and lonesome: so is the will of the conscientious.
plain: The honest, independent mind gives up easy comfort and ends up fearless and alone.

text: How did I ever bear it? How did I survive and surmount such wounds? How did my soul rise again out of those sepulchres?
plain: Look back at what you already got through. You did survive it.

text: Yea, something invulnerable, unburiable is with me, something that would rend rocks asunder: it is called MY WILL. Silently doth it proceed, and unchanged throughout the years.
plain: Something in you can't be buried or broken. It's your will, and it keeps going.

text: Yea, thou art still for me the demolisher of all graves: Hail to thee, my Will! And only where there are graves are there resurrections.
plain: You can only rise again after something has been lost. Your will gets you up.

text: And this heard I secondly: Whatever cannot obey itself, is commanded. Such is the nature of living things.
plain: If you can't command yourself, someone else will do it for you.

text: Wherever I found a living thing, there found I Will to Power; and even in the will of the servant found I the will to be master.
plain: Everything alive wants to grow stronger. Even the person serving wants to be in charge.

text: Whatever I create, and however much I love it,—soon must I be adverse to it, and to my love: so willeth my will.
plain: You'll outgrow even your best work. Let yourself move past it.

text: And he who hath to be a creator in good and evil—verily, he hath first to be a destroyer, and break values in pieces.
plain: Making your own rules means first breaking the ones you were given.

text: Let us SPEAK thereof, ye wisest ones, even though it be bad. To be silent is worse; all suppressed truths become poisonous.
plain: Say the hard thing. The truth you swallow turns toxic.

text: Calm is the bottom of my sea: who would guess that it hideth droll monsters!
plain: A calm surface can hide plenty going on underneath. Don't judge by the look of things.

text: To stand with relaxed muscles and with unharnessed will: that is the hardest for all of you, ye sublime ones!
plain: For driven people, the hard thing is letting go and just standing at ease.

text: Verily, I have often laughed at the weaklings, who think themselves good because they have crippled paws!
plain: Being harmless because you're weak isn't goodness.

text: The virtue of the pillar shalt thou strive after: more beautiful doth it ever become, and more graceful—but internally harder and more sustaining—the higher it riseth.
plain: Be like a pillar: the higher you go, the more graceful on the outside and the harder inside.

text: And from no one do I want beauty so much as from thee, thou powerful one: let thy goodness be thy last self-conquest.
plain: If you get strong, the last thing to master is being kind with it.
